corpus.note: The row carries the exact bytes MouthPromptV4 produces. The trainer uses system and input verbatim and reconstructs nothing, so what is trained on is byte-identical to what the shipping renderer will emit.

baseModel.note: Identical base and revision to run-1a/1b/1c. Holding the base fixed is what makes the Run-1c comparison a measurement of the corpus and the prompt format rather than of the weights underneath.

deviations.reason: Measured, not chosen. 73.6% of Run-2 training rows exceed 1024 tokens (median 1047, max 1294), because a plan/4 prompt carries a rendered context packet and a transcript window where plan/2 carried neither. Truncation removes the END of the sequence, which is the target, so training at 1024 would have discarded the supervised span on three rows in four. 1536 covers every row in all four splits with headroom; no row is truncated.
Run-2 has 1,616 training rows against run-1c's 730, so an epoch is 202 optimizer steps rather than 91. Evaluating every 20 keeps roughly ten checkpoints per epoch to select from.

deviations.run1cValue: none - run-1 trained a fixed number of steps deliberately
deviations.run2Value: select the checkpoint with the lowest validation loss; stop after 3 evaluations without a 0.002 improvement
deviations.reason: Requested for Run-2. Selection and stopping read mouth-v2-validation only; test and hard-eval are not opened until the checkpoint is fixed.

deviations.run1cValue: unset - relied on the PyTorch default and emitted a warning
deviations.reason: Set explicitly. The non-reentrant implementation is the supported one and composes correctly with the frozen-base/trainable-adapter split; leaving it to a default that PyTorch is in the middle of changing makes the run depend on the torch version rather than on the config.
A distinct run gets a distinct seed, recorded here so the run is reproducible from this file alone.

Same optimizer mathematically - 8-bit AdamW - without unified-memory offload. Paging exists to survive OOM on a small card: run-1 trained on a 6 GB GTX 1660 where it mattered, while this run peaks at 5.9 GB on a 12 GB RTX 5070, so it buys nothing here. It also stopped working. After the display driver reset mid-run, every subsequent attempt died in bitsandbytes' paged-memory path with an uncatchable C++ 'initialization error' - four supervised attempts with backoff to 360s, plus a direct probe with the real 4-bit model resident. The non-paged optimizer was verified over three steps on the same model in the same session and runs cleanly.

evaluation.instrument: tools/Companion.MouthFactory DeterministicChecks - the same frozen gate the corpus was built against
evaluation.beforeTraining: untouched base evaluated on validation and preserved
evaluation.afterCheckpointSelection: one evaluation on mouth-v2-test and mouth-v2-hard-eval

knownCorpusDefect.issue: The frozen JSONL files carry a UTF-8 BOM, so json.loads fails on the first line of each file for any reader that does not use utf-8-sig.
knownCorpusDefect.handling: Readers here open with utf-8-sig. The corpus is approved and frozen at e07d9d5 and was NOT modified; this is recorded for the next freeze.
